t: This is Regent's Park, one of the Royal Parks of London. It covers 410 acres, with a large central parkland and an ornamental lake, and London Zoo is among the places on its edge. The park is named for George the Fourth, who was Prince Regent before he became king. John Nash designed it. Others have connections here too. Joan Beauchamp Procter, the first female Curator of Reptiles at London Zoo, died here. So did the geologist Maria Gordon. The tennis player Frank Hadow, who won Wimbledon in 1878, was born here.
